def even_position(lst):
    """
    Checks whether every element at an even index (0, 2, 4...) 
    contains an even number.
    
    Note: In programming contexts involving lists, "even position" usually refers to indices divisible by 2 (0-based indexing).
    Index 0 is the first item, Index 1 is the second, etc.
    
    Args:
        lst (list): The list of integers to check.
        
    Returns:
        bool: True if all elements at even indices are even numbers; False otherwise.
    """
    # Iterate through the list with a step of 2 starting from index 0
    for i in range(0, len(lst), 2):
        if lst[i] % 2 != 0:
            return False
    return True

# Test cases based on your requirement and additional edge cases
assert even_position([3, 2, 1]) == False # Index 0 is 3 (odd) -> Returns False
assert even_position([4, 5, 6]) == True  # Index 0 is 4 (even), Index 2 is 6 (even) -> Returns True
assert even_position([]) == True         # Empty list has no violations -> Returns True
assert even_position([1]) == False       # Only index 0 exists and it is odd -> Returns False
assert even_position([2, 3, 4, 5]) == True # Index 0 (2), Index 2 (4) are even -> Returns True

print("All assertions passed!")

def even_position(lst):

    Checks whether every element at an even index (0, 2, 4...) 
    contains an even number.
    
    Note: In programming contexts involving lists, "even position" usually refers to indices divisible by 2 (0-based indexing).

    Args:
        lst (list): The list of integers to check.
        
    Returns:
        bool: True if all elements at even indices are even numbers; False otherwise.
    """
    # Iterate through the list with a step of 2 starting from index 0
    for i in range(0, len(lst), 2):

# Test cases based on your requirement and additional edge cases
assert even_position([3, 2, 1]) == False # Index 0 is 3 (odd) -> Returns False
